import nki
import nki.isa as nisa
import nki.language as nl

@nki.jit
def tensor_avgpool_kernel(x, pool_size):
    C, H, W = x.shape
    p = pool_size
    out_shape = (C, H // p, W // p)
    out = nl.ndarray(out_shape, dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    tile = nl.ndarray((128, 128), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=tile, src=x)
    for c in nl.affine_range(C):
        for h in nl.affine_range(H // p):
            for w in nl.affine_range(W // p):
                tile_view = tile[c, h*p:(h+1)*p, w*p:(w+1)*p]
                tile_view = nl.reshape(tile_view, (p, p))
                out[c, h, w] = nl.sum(tile_view, axis=[0, 1]) / (p * p)
    return out

On C,H,W=(32, 32, 32) pool=2: raised AssertionError: dma_copy requires src and dst to have the same number of elements, got src=32768, dst=16384 The tile you allocated holds 16384 elements but you copied 32768 into it. nisa.dma_copy does not slice or broadcast: allocate the destination with EXACTLY the shape of the slice you are moving. If you want a 128x512 piece of a bigger tensor, write t = nl.ndarray((128, 512), dtype=a.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf) and then nisa.dma_copy(dst=t, src=a[0:128, 0:512]) -- the slice on the right must have the same shape as the tile on the left.

    p = pool_size
    out_shape = (C, H // p, W // p)
    out = nl.ndarray(out_shape, dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    tile = nl.ndarray((128, 128), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=tile, src=x[0:128, 0:128])
    for c in nl.affine_range(C):
        for h in nl.affine_range(H // p):
            for w in nl.affine_range(W // p):
